displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest cumulative theistic case is a modest comparative claim: a necessary personal ground may jointly render contingency, cosmic intelligibility, moral normativity, and the relevant historical evidence less surprising than the leading naturalistic package does.

novelty.explanation: This repairs overstatement by recasting the live cumulative case as a limited comparative inference.

premises.text: The evidential contributions should be assessed conditionally and cumulatively, with dependence among observations discounted rather than assuming either strict independence or automatic aggregation.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the aggregation qualification left implicit in the original probability framework.

premises.text: A successful contingency argument must compare a personal necessary ground with the strongest natural necessary terminus instead of treating divine identification as immediate.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the modal identification gap exposed by the natural terminus objection.

premises.text: Fine-tuning supports design only to the extent that specified design expectations outperform defensible multiverse measures, generating dynamics, and observer-selection effects.

novelty.explanation: This replaces an eliminative trilemma with an explicit comparative-likelihood requirement.

premises.text: A divine moral-grounding account must explain authority through necessary perfect character while also showing why secular moral realism lacks comparable explanatory resources.

novelty.explanation: This retains the necessary-character response while addressing its remaining authority and comparison burdens.

premises.text: The resurrection case should compare source-specific likelihoods for a carefully defined historical dataset, allowing composite ordinary hypotheses and accounting explicitly for antecedent probability.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the historical comparison by adding priors, composite rivals, and source-specific analysis.

conclusion.text: If these comparisons favor one coherent personal-ground hypothesis after dependence and uncertainty are included, the combined evidence would provide defeasible support for theism, though not certainty or a complete demonstration of specifically Christian doctrine.

novelty.explanation: This proportionate conclusion preserves cumulative support while expressly limiting its evidential reach.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain coherence test
newArguments.text: A cumulative case gains force when one independently specified hypothesis predicts patterns across domains without being repeatedly modified to fit each observation. Theism could therefore be tested for cross-domain coherence: whether the same account of a rational, morally perfect, purposive ground generates expectations concerning intelligible laws, conscious reasoners, normative obligations, and historically meaningful action. This does not assume independence or guarantee success. It creates a disciplined comparison against a naturalistic package whose separate components may also combine coherently but incur their own complexity and coordination costs.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new model-comparison test based on cross-domain coherence and coordination costs.

newArguments.title: Modal profile comparison
newArguments.text: The contingency dispute can be improved by comparing modal profiles rather than labels. A candidate terminus should explain why contingent reality exists, why the governing structure has its particular capacities, and why the terminus is not merely temporally everlasting but noncontingent. A personal ground would gain an advantage only if agency explains the selection of contingent structures without importing equal unexplained complexity. A natural terminus would gain an advantage if its necessity follows from a credible theory. This framework prevents both sides from defining their preferred terminus into victory.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the shared tendency to stipulate rather than demonstrate the terminus's modal status.

thesis.text: The strongest naturalistic case is that the cited observations remain too underdetermined, dependent, or naturally tractable to discriminate reliably for a divine personal cause over a pluralistic package of physical, moral, and historical explanations.

novelty.explanation: This repairs an overly restrictive empirical standard by advancing comparative underdetermination instead.

premises.text: The affirmative bears a comparative burden, but admissible evidence may include philosophical and historical reasoning as long as it discriminates between specified hypotheses.

novelty.explanation: This repairs empirical exclusivity while retaining a demanding and neutral discrimination standard.

premises.text: A local cosmic beginning or unexplained physical boundary does not identify a divine cause when wider natural structures remain live and the boundary's ontology is unknown.

novelty.explanation: This extends the natural cosmology reply without claiming that a particular model is established.

premises.text: Apparent fine-tuning cannot strongly discriminate for design until rival generating dynamics, selection effects, measures, and the expectations of a specified designer are comparatively evaluated.

novelty.explanation: This repairs possibility listing by requiring symmetric likelihood comparisons for every hypothesis.

premises.text: The divine moral account faces an unresolved authority question, while secular moral realism remains a live ontology distinct from evolutionary explanations of moral cognition.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the conflation of moral psychology with ontology and strengthens the independence objection.

premises.text: Resurrection reports require source-specific historical analysis, and ordinary composite explanations retain a major prior advantage unless their likelihood for the full evidence is demonstrably negligible.

novelty.explanation: This turns a list of possibilities into a structured prior-and-likelihood comparison.

conclusion.text: Unless the affirmative demonstrates robust comparative advantages across these domains after uncertainty, dependence, priors, and strong natural alternatives are included, withholding the conclusion that the greater evidential weight supports God remains proportionate.

novelty.explanation: This extends the burden argument as a limited withholding conclusion rather than a disproof of God.

newArguments.title: Evidential dependence audit
newArguments.text: The cumulative case may overstate its force if several observations arise from the same deeper facts or interpretive commitments. Cosmic beginning and contingency may share assumptions about ultimate explanation; moral experience and perceived purpose may share human agency-detection tendencies; resurrection judgments may depend upon prior openness to miracle. A formal dependence audit would group correlated evidence, test conclusions under alternative priors, and prevent repeated counting. If support for theism remains stable after those adjustments, it is stronger; if it collapses, apparent breadth was not equivalent to independent confirmation.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new sensitivity analysis for dependence and correlated evidential interpretation.

newArguments.title: Symmetric specification principle
newArguments.text: Comparative explanation should require equal specificity from divine and natural hypotheses. A vague designer can accommodate almost any constants, moral order, or historical outcome, just as an unspecified multiverse can accommodate almost any universe. Both sides should state mechanisms, probability distributions, scope, and potential disconfirming observations at comparable resolution. Penalizing only natural models for missing details while allowing flexible divine intentions would distort the comparison; penalizing only theism while accepting an undefined multiverse would do the same. Symmetric specification makes the dispute more rigorous without presupposing either conclusion.

novelty.explanation: This repairs asymmetric model criticism by imposing the same specification burden on both sides.
